"I've had to fight myself every day to remind myself that I had a father. He existed. He lived with me. I knew him... It's not just in my head." Syrian activist @WafaMustafa9 tells me about her search for the truth about her father, imprisoned under Assad. "I hope my dad knows... that I will not give up on him."

Video

"The Syria that we hope to see is a Syria where it's equal, it's safe, there's freedom of speech." Filmmakers @waadalkateab and @WafaMustafa9 tell me about their hopes and demands for post-Assad Syria. Many families still don't know what happened to their loved ones, what Wafa calls "the violence of waiting."

"My father, Ali Mustafa... he was a very, very powerful, very tough guy, but he was also at the same time very kind." Filmmaker and activist @WafaMustafa9 tells me about her father, a political prisoner in Assad's Syria. Her documentary Maybe Tomorrow chronicles her search for the truth about what happened to him.

During the Obama administration, “the president wisely made the choice not to agree to Prime Minister Netanyahu's request to be able to go in and bomb and to even join in the bombing,” his former top diplomat John Kerry tells me. “Obama said, ‘No, we're going to try diplomacy.’”

Video
